title: Brentwood
intro: An Essex market town between two country parks, with a medieval chapel ruin on its high street and a classical cathedral finished in 1991.

items.name: Weald Country Park
items.blurb: A former deer park with lakes, woods and open grassland on the west side of Brentwood, with a herd of deer and a visitor centre.
items.tip: Walk up to the top of the park for the view.

items.name: Thorndon Country Park
items.blurb: Ancient woodland, meadows and lakes on the old Thorndon estate south of Brentwood, with views from the hill over the Thames estuary.
items.tip: The southern park has the lakes; the northern woods have bluebells in spring.

items.name: Brentwood Cathedral
items.blurb: A Roman Catholic cathedral in a classical style designed by Quinlan Terry and completed in 1991, light and white inside.

credit.author: Fr James Bradley from Washington, DC

items.name: Thomas Becket Chapel ruins
items.blurb: The ruined walls of a medieval chapel dedicated to Thomas Becket, on the High Street where pilgrims once passed on the way to Canterbury.
items.tip: A quick stop on the High Street.

items.name: Ingatestone Hall
items.blurb: A Tudor manor house built in the 1540s for Sir William Petre and still owned by his family, with gardens and opening days in summer.
items.tip: Check the summer opening days before you go.
